evidence: Vitruvius 10.1.1: tignīs statūtīs et trānsversāriīs conligātīs
terms.comment: One noun serves both horizontal functions; Latin does not distinguish ledger and transom.
Morgan–Owens and Traupman record it in gymnastics; applying it to this scaffold bar is our contextual extension. The classical member name is trānsversārium.

phrases.latin: Theodōrus bacillum aduncum ex trānsversāriō māchinae suspendit.
phrases.english: Theo hung the hooked stick from the scaffold’s crossbar.

sources: Lewis & Short: transversarius · Lewis & Short: transversus · Morgan–Owens: horizontal bar (gymnastics) · Lewis & Short: suspendo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 329.
